issue.title: BBS nodes / Store and Forward
issue.body:
Might be worth exploring the installation of BBS nodes using micro controllers like nRF52 etc... to temporarily store messages and sync with anyone walking past. <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulletin_board_system>

Even better if you allow for messages to hop between BBS nodes.

You might need these nodes to have an SD card so that you have enough space to do a store and forward capability.

This would allow for more persistent communications with threads by allowing passerby to do an active sync of particular messages from a thread (but at a cost to anonymity as the BBS node if compromised will be able to tell that someone near the area is trying to access specific kind of messages)

`handle(_:)` performs a single `connection.receive(...)` and immediately decodes that chunk as a complete JSON request. TCP does not preserve write boundaries, so fragmented requests can arrive in multiple chunks; in that case this decodes partial JSON and returns an `invalid service request` error even for valid client payloads.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Kill the actual service process on startup timeout**

On startup timeout, the code always calls `_terminate_process(proc.pid)`, but in `bundle-open` mode `proc` is the short-lived `/usr/bin/open` process, not the launched harness app PID discovered in `pid`. If the app was launched but never became ready, this path removes metadata while leaving the real service running in the background, causing orphaned processes and inconsistent subsequent `status/start/stop` behavior.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind harness listener to loopback only**

`start(port:)` creates a plain `NWListener` on the requested port without constraining the local interface/address, which means the control socket is reachable from non-local interfaces even though the log says `127.0.0.1`. Because this endpoint accepts unauthenticated control commands (`send`, `command`, `nickname_set`, etc.), exposing it beyond loopback is a security risk in any environment where the host is network-accessible.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The CLI advertises `--to` as accepting a peer nickname or peer ID, but the live runtime resolver only matches nicknames from `getPeerNicknames()`. When a caller passes a valid peer ID, private send returns `'<id>' not found` even though the target peer exists. This breaks a documented input path for private messaging in live mode.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Buffer TCP request until full JSON line arrives**

The live service decodes whatever bytes arrive in a single `NWConnection.receive` callback as a complete request, but TCP is a byte stream and can split one logical message across multiple receives. In that case, `dispatch` gets partial JSON and returns an error, so valid live commands can fail intermittently under normal network behavior. The handler should accumulate bytes until a full delimiter (newline) or connection completion before decoding.

issue.title: Feature Request: Windows client support
issue.body:
Summary
There is currently no Windows client for bitchat. This limits adoption for users who rely on Windows as their primary desktop OS and want to participate in the mesh network without needing an Apple device.
Current state
Bitchat is available on iOS and macOS. The codebase appears to be Swift-based, which ties it tightly to Apple platforms.
Request
Add a Windows-compatible client, either as:

A native port using a cross-platform language (e.g. Rust, Go, or Flutter), or
A standalone Windows application that implements the same Bluetooth LE mesh protocol

Why this matters

Windows holds the majority desktop market share globally
Users without Apple hardware are fully excluded from the network, which weakens the mesh
A cross-platform implementation would also make future Linux support more feasible

Notes

Windows has Bluetooth LE support via the Windows.Devices.Bluetooth API (available from Windows 10 v1703+)
A protocol spec or documentation of the mesh layer would help third-party contributors attempt a Windows client independently
Happy to help test on Windows 10/11 if development starts

issue.title: Proposal: SDK packages for the BitChat protocol
issue.body:
## What

I've built and published a set of SDK packages that implement the BitChat binary
protocol and Nostr transport layer:

### npm ([protocol-core](https://github.com/bitchat-sdk/protocol-core-js) · [nostr](https://github.com/bitchat-sdk/nostr-js))
```sh
npm install @bitchat-sdk/protocol-core  # Binary encode/decode, TLV codec, peer ID utils
npm install @bitchat-sdk/nostr           # Nostr relay client, NIP-17 gift wrap, packet embedding
```

### PyPI ([protocol-core](https://github.com/bitchat-sdk/protocol-core-py) · [nostr](https://github.com/bitchat-sdk/nostr-py))
```sh
pip install bitchat-protocol  # Binary encode/decode, TLV codec, peer ID utils
pip install bitchat-nostr     # Nostr relay client, NIP-17 gift wrap, packet embedding
```

### Swift Package Manager ([BitchatProtocol](https://github.com/bitchat-sdk/BitchatProtocol) · [BitchatNostr](https://github.com/bitchat-sdk/BitchatNostr))
```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/bitchat-sdk/BitchatProtocol", from: "0.1.0")  // Binary codec
.package(url: "https://github.com/bitchat-sdk/BitchatNostr", from: "0.1.0")     // Nostr integration
```

All packages are wire-compatible with the current BitChat iOS and Android apps.
They're tested against a shared golden vector fixture suite that verifies
encode/decode parity across all three languages.

## What's included

- Protocol v1 and v2 header support
- Compression (raw deflate) with bomb detection
- TLV codec for AnnouncementPacket and PrivateMessagePacket
- NIP-17 gift wrap (seal → wrap → send, receive → unwrap → unseal)
- Relay client with reconnect, observability hooks, and metrics counters
- 100+ tests per language (unit, fixtures, fuzz)
- Cross-language golden vector fixtures
- CI workflow (GitHub Actions) for JS (Node 18/20/22), Python (3.10-3.12), Swift (5.9/5.10)

## What I'm proposing

I'd like to contribute these as an official part of the BitChat project — either as:

1. **A directory in this repo** (e.g. `ecosystem/packages/`) with its own CI job, or
2. **A separate repo** under the permissionlesstech org (e.g. `permissionlesstech/bitchat-sdk`)

Happy to do either. The packages are self-contained, don't touch any existing code,
and I'll maintain them going forward (tracking protocol changes and publishing updates).

Open to feedback on the approach before I put up a PR.
